newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Osprey Maritime seeks Sing-dollar listing.
newsitem.headline: Osprey Maritime seeks Sing-dollar listing.

text.p: Osprey Maritime Ltd has approached the Stock Exchange of Singapore to change its listing from U.S. to Singapore dollars, chairman Tim Cottew told Reuters on Thursday.
"It would be good...we are now a Singapore company," Cottew said of the oil tanker charter company which was set up in 1990 and was listed on the Singapore Stock Exchange in 1994.

"The reason the listing is in U.S. dollars is that we were considered to be a U.S. company. But having been in Singapore...and more than met the Exchange's requirements, we approached the Stock Exchange to find out whether we would be considered (for a Singapore-dollar listing)," he said.

Cottew said Osprey Maritime's "informal approach" was made some months back and prior to Finance Minister Richard Hu's announcement in October that foreign companies listed in Singapore could convert their shares into Singapore-dollar denominated stocks, provided they met certain conditions.

Among the criteria are that the company must be incorporated in Singapore and have at least two years operating track record here and it must have more than 35 percent of revenue, profits or expenses attributable to its Singapore operations.
But Cottew said so far there has been no reply from the Stock Exchange.
"I don't believe we will see a change in the situation," he said.
"U.S. (denominated) stocks are moving quite well...perhaps the Stock Exchange wants a reasonable contingent," he added.
Singapore-dollar denominated stocks usually have better trading liquidity compared to foreign currency-denominated stocks listed in Singapore.
Cottew said he was not happy with Osprey's current trading liquidity as most shares "were fairly closely held" by mainly institutional investors.
Although it was difficult to speculate whether liquidity would improve with a switch to Singapore-dollar listing, Cottew said the average investor would at least have more access.
